sections.title: Frequently Asked Questions

items.q: What class of insulated gloves do I need?
items.a: Glove class depends on the maximum voltage you work with. Class 00 covers up to 500V AC, Class 0 up to 1,000V AC, and Class 2 up to 17,000V AC. Always select gloves rated above your working voltage.

items.q: How often should insulated gloves be tested?
items.a: OSHA and ASTM D120 require insulated gloves to be electrically tested every 6 months. Gloves must also be visually inspected before each use.

items.q: Is arc-rated clothing the same as flame-resistant clothing?
items.a: All arc-rated clothing is flame-resistant, but not all FR clothing is arc-rated. Arc-rated garments have a specific cal/cm² rating tested per ASTM F1959 for arc flash protection.

items.a: Yes. FR clothing is required in areas where thermal runaway, cell venting, or arc flash from high-voltage DC systems is possible. This includes formation testing, pack assembly, and storage areas.

items.q: What respiratory protection is needed for battery off-gas events?
items.a: Multi-gas cartridge respirators protect against HF, CO, and SO₂ during minor venting events. SCBA is required for thermal runaway emergencies where gas concentrations are immediately dangerous.

items.q: Can you supply PPE kits for battery gigafactory operations?
items.a: Yes. We assemble zone-specific PPE kits for battery production lines including chemical-resistant gloves, ESD clothing, respirators, and electrical PPE for each manufacturing stage.
